source: 23-case corpus (A1-A15, B1-B8) supplied for span-surprise/salience conformance testing
discipline: Every case is tagged with a TIER: engine (structural, no world knowledge, detectable by nul/temporality/rowForm/scriptProfile/received), model (requires semantic or world knowledge the material does not itself carry — correct engine behavior is a typed gap, never a lucky hit), mixed (part of the case is structural, part is not), or out-of-scope (the signal lives on an axis no mechanism here exposes — A7's acrostic).

For model-tier cases the fixture still runs the same structural detector the case superficially resembles, and the expected verdict is whatever was ACTUALLY OBSERVED when it was run — including a structural echo where one exists (e.g. a confession sentence differing in length from surrounding imperative sentences). A model-tier label is a claim about what would be required to correctly INTERPRET the signal, not a guarantee that no structural byproduct exists.
expectedVerdict values are locked from a real run of goldens/surprise/score.mjs, not hand-asserted — see README.md for the run that produced them.

cases.notes: REVISED from out-of-scope. A general axis-sweep now exists (projectionVerdict): candidate axes are 'character at position k of every row', unprivileged, k=0..25. Without a witness, this correctly REFUSES (insufficient_material) rather than guessing -- 6-character projected strings have no statistical power. With a received lexicon (a dictionary is a witness prior exactly like Benford's Law or a coref prior, named and provenanced), pos0 decodes to FIND+ME via word-break segmentation, since FINDME is not itself a dictionary word. Uniquely selective: 1 of 26 axes segments into substantial (3+ letter) dictionary words, verified against a negative control of random text (0 of 29 axes) and against two 2-letter-word false positives caught and filtered by requiring at least one substantial word per segmentation.

observed.finding: THE decisive case: burstiness only ever selects the highest windowed mean and compares it to a null of highest means, so a LOW-value anomaly (a fast time) can never even be the observation tested. Structurally invisible to every organ in this codebase using the standard one-sided pattern, not just this probe.

observedRunNote: Verdicts in each case's `observed` field are from a real execution of goldens/surprise/score.mjs against detectors.mjs, run 2026-07-31. Two real bugs were caught and fixed during this run and are recorded in README.md: numericVerdict originally required BOTH the high- and low-side grounds to succeed, discarding a real high-side signal (B4) when the unrelated low side degenerated; A12 was originally scoped to a script-family detector, which is structurally blind to a same-script language switch (French/English both Latin) and was corrected to a letter-trigram profile distance.
